children: Kering SA (EURONEXT:KER) says a supply‑chain and supplier consolidation is underway and manufacturing will remain in Italy as it reshapes brands like Saint Laurent and Gucci, but uneven recovery, China headwinds and weaker Gucci demand keep analysts cautious and the firm on a sell view.
: Berenberg says Kering SA (KER) is in early turnaround: restructuring underway, uneven brand recovery, Chinese and aspirational consumer headwinds could affect revival; firm keeps sell rating.
: Bernstein warns Kering (KER) may see slower Q3 momentum, citing China as the main headwind and weaker Gucci demand; KER shares slid about 2% on the report.
: Kering SA (KER) said Saint Laurent revenue dropped ~6% last year, then resumed growth in H1 this year, reported in the group’s brand performance update.

: Kering SA (KER) is restructuring its supply chain to cut fragmentation and simplify tiers after 25% of suppliers account for 98% of sourcing, aiming to consolidate suppliers and streamline sourcing.
: Kering SA (KER) said it will keep manufacturing in Italy, with no plans to move production abroad, affirming Italy remains central to its supply chain and current Italian operations.
: Kering SA (KER) said it won’t buy a minority stake in Armani, noting Giorgio Armani’s will didn’t name Kering and the company is focused on other priorities.
: Kering (KER) said Gucci might make some sneakers in China for technical needs but has no plans to move overall production, clarifying its manufacturing stance for the brand.
